intro: A heat warning gives one number: the air temperature in the shade. A family under a tin roof lives with four heats at once, and the worst of it often comes after dark.

heats.name: Outdoor air
heats.text: The temperature a weather station measures, in the shade. It is the number in almost every heat warning, but not what people feel inside a tin-roofed room.

heats.name: The roof
heats.text: Sun-baked sheet metal gets far hotter than the air. Roofs of informal homes in Mumbai and Pune measured above 50 °C when the air was about 30 °C.

source.label: Urban Solutions: how informal settlements stay cool (informal measurements)

heats.name: Radiant heat
heats.text: A hot ceiling gives off heat onto the people below, like standing near a stove, so a room can feel hotter than its air. This is what mean radiant temperature measures.

heats.name: Indoor air
heats.text: The air inside, held in by thin walls, few windows and crowded rooms.

night.text: After sunset the street starts to cool, but thin-roofed homes cool slowly. In low-income homes measured in Dhaka, Delhi, Faisalabad and rural Maharashtra, temperatures in tin-roofed houses swung 3–4 °C more over the month than the outdoor air, and stayed warmer indoors because they cooled so slowly at night.

source.label: Tasgaonkar et al., Scientific Data, 2022: indoor heat in low-income homes in South Asia

facts.text: hotter, at most, for people in Ahmedabad’s informal settlements than for people in formal housing, in a survey of 860 households.
hotter indoors than outside, in pilot measurements in informal settlements in Kenya, Tanzania and Zimbabwe.
cooler indoors under reflective roof paint than under ordinary roofs, in Ahmedabad’s informal settlements.

source.label: NRDC: community-led cool roofs in four Indian cities

nuance.text: Indoors is not always hotter at midday: in an experiment in The Gambia, metal-roofed houses were about 1.4 °C cooler than the outdoor shade by day, but warmer at night. The danger is nights that do not cool.

source.label: Malaria Journal, 2021: roof colour and indoor temperature in rural Gambia

plans: Heat warnings measure the street. Heat plans can protect the room too: count indoor and night-time heat, warn for hot nights, and pay for cooler roofs where people sleep.
